prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: In the first four frames, the camera wearer sits looking down at a tiled floor, holding a vertical twine-wrapped cardboard tube with both hands in the foreground (~0.3–0.4 m away) above their crossed legs (~0.4–0.5 m). On the floor in front (~0.7–1.2 m away, all within or near extended arm's reach) sit a twine ball on the left, a smaller upright cardboard cylinder in the middle, a glue gun and scissors to the right, a long draft stopper along the base of a glass door (~1.2–1.5 m), and an open wooden box on the far right (~1.0–1.3 m). A cat enters on the upper right in frame 2 (~1.3 m away, facing left and looking sideways relative to the wearer), walks left in frame 3 (~1.1 m), turns away toward the glass door in frame 4 (~1.1 m), and stands upright against the glass in frame 5 (~0.8–1.0 m) as the camera wearer tilts their head up and reaches their right arm out (~0.3–0.8 m) to touch the cat's lower back while the held tube drops out of view. The depth map clearly separates the elevated foreground tube and arms from the slanted floor plane and captures the hollow interior depth of the smaller cylinder, which is less obvious in flat RGB. However, the depth map is unreliable on the glass door pane in frame 5—rendering the translucent frosted window as a pitch-black infinite void—and loses thin structures like the loose twine and electrical cord on the floor.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates discrete foreground entities against the unlabelled background floor, identifying the camera wearer's lower body and arms at the bottom (~0.3–0.5 m away), the small upright cylinder ahead (~0.9 m, mislabelled as 'cup' in all 5 frames), the glue gun to its right (~0.8 m, mislabelled as 'scissors' in frame 4), and the cat in the upper right (~0.8–1.3 m away across frames 2–5). Across frames 1 to 4, the wearer's hands and crossed legs remain in the bottom foreground within immediate reach while the cat enters from the far right behind the wooden box (frame 2), steps leftward in front of the door (frame 3), sits facing the door (frame 4), and rears up on the glass door as the wearer's right arm extends forward to make contact with its torso (frame 5). The masks clearly trace the silhouette shift of the cat's movement and the spatial boundary between the wearer's reaching arm and the cat's body in frame 5. However, the map is highly unreliable in class and instance consistency: it splits the single camera wearer into two separate 'person' instances (left and right sides) in frames 1–4, misclassifies the cat as a 'dog' in frame 3 and as a 'person' in frame 5, labels the frosted glass window as a 'tv' in frame 5, and completely misses the prominent twine-wrapped tube occluding the center of frames 1–4 as well as the twine ball, actual scissors, and wooden box.
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders only 2D magenta hand skeletons for the camera wearer's left and right hands in the lower center of frames 1, 3, and 4 (~0.3–0.4 m from the camera) and the extended right hand in the upper right of frame 5 (~0.7–0.8 m away), with no yellow body keypoints detected in any frame because only the wearer's lower limbs and forearms are in the field of view. In frames 1, 3, and 4, the two hands are positioned symmetrically about 0.1–0.15 m apart around the vertical cardboard tube, with thumbs pointing inward toward each other and fingers curving around the cylinder's sides, showing subtle grip adjustments while the fingertips are partly occluded behind the tube. In frame 5, the left hand leaves the frame while the right hand shifts upward and forward toward the cat's lower back, oriented palm-down with fingers spread and pointing up and left at contact distance. This skeleton rendering makes the exact finger articulation, thumb opposition, and palm orientation around the held cylinder much clearer than in the RGB or depth images. However, the map is unreliable in frame 2 where both hands are completely missed despite being clearly visible in the same pose as frames 1 and 3, and it provides no skeletal tracking for the wearer's forearms/legs or for the cat.
